first_impression.reaction: Googled 'mauritius wedding' on the train. The intro answers 'will it count?' straight away and gives the whole process in one sentence: send documents to Port Louis, get originals checked when you land, 24-hour publication, marry. That's fast. But the title and intro are all about Australians, and I'm in Singapore, so I spent a second wondering if this applies to me at all. The Key Takeaways are clean. I jumped to the document list, then the 'In Port Louis' bit, then the FAQ. Bookmarked. What I still don't know: how much it costs and how many days I actually need on the island before the wedding.

journey.quote: Mauritius is on the shortlist, and before you fall for a lagoon you want to know one thing: will the marriage count? It will.
journey.reaction: Direct yes in the first two lines. Good, no fluff.

journey.quote: A Mauritius wedding is legally binding for two Australians when it follows the Civil Status Division's process for two non-citizens.
journey.reaction: For two Australians. I'm not Australian. The process is for 'two non-citizens', so probably me too, but the page never says so outright.

journey.quote: Your application must reach the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis at least one month before the wedding, with documents forwarded 6 to 8 weeks ahead.
journey.reaction: The actual deadline, with numbers. That's what I'd screenshot.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Mauritius?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the Civil Status Division sets out a dedicated process for the marriage of two non-citizens who are also non-residents, which is where most Australian couples flying in for their wedding sit.
journey.reaction: Dated, and it links to the government page. That handles my 'is this still true?' worry.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Start with the travel side, because it has its own rules and they can move.
journey.reaction: Smartraveller, visas, yellow fever, the Australian High Commission. Four paragraphs before the document list, and most of it isn't for me. Scrolled past on my phone.

journey.section: What the Civil Status Division asks for
journey.quote: Two photocopies of each birth certificate, drawn up in English or French and issued not more than 3 months earlier.
journey.reaction: Bold-led list, and the 3-month birth certificate detail is something I'd never have guessed. Really useful.

journey.quote: Ask the Civil Status Office which days and hours to come in, and how many working days to allow between landing and the ceremony, then book your flights around the answer.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I needed, how early to fly in, and the answer is 'ask them'. I get that the page may not know, but it's a letdown.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much. 'A fee applies' with no number.

journey.quote: Cyclone season runs from November to May, Smartraveller says, but cyclones can occur at any time of year
journey.reaction: Specific, sourced, and the kind of thing you'd want before picking a month. Good.

journey.quote: Yes. Two witnesses must be present at the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Straight yes. The FAQ answers the follow-ups I'd have Googled next.

journey.section: Plan your Mauritius wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Sales bit, fine. 'Quotes in AUD' confirms it's an Australian company. No idea what anything costs.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask the Civil Status Office which days and hours to come in, and how many working days to allow between landing and the ceremony, then book your flights around the answer.
turn_offs_found.why: How early to arrive is the practical question behind the whole process, and both the section and the FAQ send me off to ask someone else. If there's any published guidance, I want it here.

turn_offs_found.quote: Start with the travel side, because it has its own rules and they can move.
turn_offs_found.why: The Smartraveller, visa, yellow fever and High Commission paragraphs sit before the document checklist. On a phone that's a lot of scrolling, mostly not relevant to me, before the list I came for.

would_share_with: My partner: the Key Takeaways and the 'What the Civil Status Division asks for' list, as screenshots

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mauritius-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for the steps and got most of them. I don't know this brand, it's clearly aimed at Australians, and I'm not choosing a planner yet. Bookmark, not enquiry.

top_3_changes: Give arrival timing a firmer answer if any source supports it, for example a typical minimum number of working days, with an 'as at' date. Otherwise say plainly in the Key Takeaways that the Office sets it, so readers know before they scroll.
Move or shorten the 'Before you go: entry and documents' travel paragraphs so the Civil Status document checklist comes sooner on mobile, for example a short travel box after the steps.

Add one line near the top saying the Civil Status steps apply to any two non-citizen visitors and only the 'Getting your certificate ready for Australia' section is Australia-specific, so non-Australian searchers don't bounce.
